---
title: "Choosing the number of components"
---

The singular values describe how well components reconstruct the training matrix. They do not determine how many components reconstruct genuinely hidden entries. The inventory-record completion target thus separates three operations: fit directions on training inventories, choose rank on validation inventories, and estimate performance once on test inventories.

## Separating fitting, selection, and evaluation

Let $\mathcal T$, $\mathcal V$, and $\mathcal E$ denote training, validation, and test inventory records. Training data determine:

1. which segment columns occur often enough to retain;
2. the segment means $\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_{\mathcal T}$;
3. the component directions $\mathbf V_{\mathcal T}$.

For a validation inventory with masked cells, scores at rank $K$ are

$$
\widehat{\mathbf t}_{i,K}
=
(\mathbf x_i^*-\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_{\mathcal T})^{\mathsf T}
\mathbf V_{\mathcal T,K},
$$

and the reconstruction is

$$
\widehat{\mathbf x}_{i,K}
=
\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_{\mathcal T}
+
\mathbf V_{\mathcal T,K}\widehat{\mathbf t}_{i,K}.
$$

The selected rank is

$$
\widehat K
=
\arg\min_{K\in\mathcal K}
L_{\mathrm{bal}}(\mathcal V,K),
$$

where

$$
L_{\mathrm{bal}}
=
\frac{1}{2n_1}\sum_{x=1}(x-\widehat x)^2
+
\frac{1}{2n_0}\sum_{x=0}(x-\widehat x)^2.
$$

The final test loss is evaluated at $\widehat K$. Test loss must not be used to revise $\mathcal K$, preprocessing, or the masking procedure. Otherwise the test set becomes another validation set, the [one-split repeated-decisions problem](../model-criticism-and-prediction/training-and-test-data.qmd#one-split-and-repeated-decisions).

## Implementing rank selection

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

balanced_loss <- function(truth, prediction, type = c("brier", "log")) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  prediction <- pmin(pmax(prediction, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6)
  cell_loss <- if (type == "brier") {
    (truth - prediction)^2
  } else {
    -(truth * log(prediction) + (1 - truth) * log(1 - prediction))
  }
  listed <- as.logical(truth)
  mean(c(
    mean(cell_loss[listed]),
    mean(cell_loss[!listed])
  ))
}

make_mask <- function(X, rows, seed, n_each = 3L) {
  set.seed(seed)
  mask <- matrix(FALSE, nrow = length(rows), ncol = ncol(X))
  for (i in seq_along(rows)) {
    present <- which(X[rows[[i]], ] == 1)
    unlisted <- which(X[rows[[i]], ] == 0)
    mask[i, c(sample(present, n_each), sample(unlisted, n_each))] <- TRUE
  }
  list(rows = rows, mask = mask)
}

reconstruct <- function(X, evaluation, mean, loadings, rank) {
  observed <- X[evaluation$rows, , drop = FALSE]
  mean_matrix <- matrix(rep(mean, each = nrow(observed)), nrow = nrow(observed))
  observed[evaluation$mask] <- mean_matrix[evaluation$mask]
  centered <- sweep(observed, 2, mean, "-")
  prediction <- mean_matrix
  if (rank > 0L) {
    directions <- loadings[, seq_len(rank), drop = FALSE]
    prediction <- prediction + centered %*% directions %*% t(directions)
  }
  pmin(pmax(prediction, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6)
}

phoible <- readRDS("data/phoible/phoible-pilot.rds")
inventories <- phoible$inventories[
  order(phoible$inventories$glottocode,
        as.integer(phoible$inventories$inventory_id)),
]
groups <- split(seq_len(nrow(inventories)), inventories$glottocode)
RNGkind(sample.kind = "Rejection")
set.seed(20260827L)
chosen <- vapply(groups, function(x) x[[sample.int(length(x), 1L)]], integer(1))
selected <- inventories[unname(chosen), ]

area <- selected$macroarea
area[is.na(area) | area == ""] <- "Unclassified"
selected$split <- NA_character_
set.seed(20261018L)
for (name in sort(unique(area))) {
  index <- sample(which(area == name))
  n_holdout <- floor(0.15 * length(index))
  selected$split[index[seq_len(n_holdout)]] <- "validation"
  selected$split[index[n_holdout + seq_len(n_holdout)]] <- "test"
  selected$split[index[is.na(selected$split[index])]] <- "training"
}
training_rows <- which(selected$split == "training")
validation_rows <- which(selected$split == "validation")
test_rows <- which(selected$split == "test")

memberships <- merge(
  phoible$memberships,
  selected[c("inventory_id", "glottocode")],
  by = c("inventory_id", "glottocode")
)
frequency <- table(
  memberships$segment_id[memberships$glottocode %in%
    selected$glottocode[training_rows]]
)
column_ids <- sort(names(frequency)[frequency >= 20L])
X <- matrix(
  0,
  nrow = nrow(selected),
  ncol = length(column_ids),
  dimnames = list(selected$glottocode, column_ids)
)
retained <- memberships[memberships$segment_id %in% column_ids, ]
X[cbind(
  match(retained$glottocode, rownames(X)),
  match(retained$segment_id, colnames(X))
)] <- 1

training_mean <- colMeans(X[training_rows, , drop = FALSE])
Z <- sweep(X[training_rows, , drop = FALSE], 2, training_mean, "-")
decomposition <- svd(Z, nu = 64L, nv = 64L)
validation <- make_mask(X, validation_rows, seed = 20261019L)
test <- make_mask(X, test_rows, seed = 20261020L)

candidate_ranks <- c(0L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 5L, 8L, 12L, 16L,
                     24L, 32L, 40L, 50L, 64L) # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting

score_rank <- function(evaluation, rank, type) {
  prediction <- reconstruct(X, evaluation, training_mean, decomposition$v, rank)
  truth <- X[evaluation$rows, , drop = FALSE][evaluation$mask]
  balanced_loss(truth, prediction[evaluation$mask], type)
}

rank_curve <- data.frame(
  rank = candidate_ranks,
  validation_brier = vapply(
    candidate_ranks, function(k) score_rank(validation, k, "brier"), numeric(1)
  ),
  validation_log = vapply(
    candidate_ranks, function(k) score_rank(validation, k, "log"), numeric(1)
  )
)
selected_rank <- rank_curve$rank[[which.min(rank_curve$validation_brier)]]
selected_rank
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4

ggplot(rank_curve, aes(x = rank, y = validation_brier)) +
  geom_line(color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(color = "grey20", size = 1.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = selected_rank, color = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.65) +
  labs(x = "Candidate rank", y = "Validation balanced Brier loss") +
  theme_classic()
```

The validation minimum occurs at rank `r selected_rank`. The line marks the result of the fixed selection rule; it is the only annotation needed to read the curve.

## Preserving one final evaluation

The code below computes the test comparison only after `selected_rank` exists.

```{r}
test_truth <- X[test$rows, , drop = FALSE][test$mask]
test_baseline <- reconstruct(X, test, training_mean, decomposition$v, 0L)[test$mask]
test_selected <- reconstruct(
  X, test, training_mean, decomposition$v, selected_rank
)[test$mask]

data.frame(
  procedure = c("training prevalence", paste0("rank ", selected_rank)),
  balanced_brier = c(
    balanced_loss(test_truth, test_baseline, "brier"),
    balanced_loss(test_truth, test_selected, "brier")
  ),
  balanced_log = c(
    balanced_loss(test_truth, test_baseline, "log"),
    balanced_loss(test_truth, test_selected, "log")
  )
)
```

The selected reconstruction reduces test balanced Brier loss from `r round(balanced_loss(test_truth, test_baseline, "brier"), 4)` to `r round(balanced_loss(test_truth, test_selected, "brier"), 4)`. Balanced log loss moves in the same direction, from `r round(balanced_loss(test_truth, test_baseline, "log"), 4)` to `r round(balanced_loss(test_truth, test_selected, "log"), 4)`.

One inventory was sampled per Glottocode, and the split is stratified by macroarea. Families were not assigned wholesale to splits. Thus this evaluation concerns held-out inventory records under broad area balance; it does not establish transfer to unseen families.

## Why other criteria answer different questions

Choosing a rank from observed training reconstruction rewards additional components by construction. A scree bend or a cumulative-variance threshold may summarize the observed matrix, but neither directly evaluates hidden cells. Conversely, validation loss is tied to the masking rule, loss function, and new-inventory target. It does not identify a true number of phonological dimensions.

Rank selection also includes preprocessing. Segment retention, centering, component fitting, and masking must remain inside their assigned partitions. Letting validation or test inventories determine retained columns would create [leakage through preprocessing](../model-criticism-and-prediction/training-and-test-data.qmd#leakage-through-preprocessing).

## Checking rank selection

1. Which quantities are fitted on training inventories?
2. Which data choose the rank?
3. Why is the test set evaluated only once?
4. Why can the training reconstruction curve not select a predictive rank?
5. What generalization claim is blocked because family is not the split unit?

The selected rank supports the IRCT, not a universal dimensionality claim. The [final page](valex-megaacceptability.qmd) moves to a supervised problem in which PCA compression itself must compete with the uncompressed linguistic predictor.
